paragraphs: This Annual Report on Form 10-K contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. Actual results, performance or achievements could differ materially from those projected in the forward-looking statements as a result of a number of risks, uncertainties, and other factors. For a discussion of important factors that could cause our results, performance, or achievements to differ materially from any future results, performance, or achievements expressed or implied by our forward-looking statements, refer to Part I, Item 1A "Risk Factors" and Part I, Item 7 "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" below. Unless the context indicates otherwise, references to "Mativ," the "Company," "we," "us," "our," or similar terms include Mativ Holdings, Inc. and our consolidated subsidiaries.

Mativ Holdings, Inc. is a global leader in specialty materials, solving our customers' most complex challenges by engineering bold, innovative solutions that connect, protect, and purify our world. Mativ manufactures globally through our family of business-to-business and consumer product brands. Mativ targets premium applications across diversified and growing end-markets, from filtration to healthcare to sustainable packaging and more. Our broad portfolio of technologies combines polymers, fibers, and resins to optimize the performance of our customers' products across multiple stages of the value chain.

Mativ was incorporated in Delaware in 1995 as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kimberly-Clark Corporation ("Kimberly-Clark"). On November 30, 1995, Kimberly-Clark transferred its tobacco-related paper and other paper products businesses conducted in the United States, France and Canada to the Company and distributed all of the outstanding shares of common stock of the Company to its stockholders (the "spin-off"). As a result, the Company became an independent public company. Over time, the Company diversified its portfolio through innovation efforts and a number of acquisitions to broaden its exposure to adjacent categories, such as filtration, specialty films, tapes, and healthcare.

On July 6, 2022, Schweitzer-Mauduit International, Inc. ("SWM") completed a merger transaction involving Neenah, Inc. ("Neenah"), pursuant to which a wholly-owned subsidiary of SWM merged with and into Neenah (the "Merger"), with Neenah surviving the Merger as a direct and wholly-owned subsidiary of SWM. Effective as of the closing date of the Merger, SWM changed its name to Mativ Holdings, Inc.

On November 30, 2023, we completed the sale of our Engineered Papers business ("EP business") to Evergreen Hill Enterprise Pte. Ltd. ("Evergreen Hill Enterprise"). With the sale of the EP business (the "EP Divestiture"), Mativ ceased participating in tobacco-based product markets.

Effective with the sale, the EP business is presented as a discontinued operation for all periods presented and certain prior period amounts have been retrospectively recast to reflect these changes. The consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto, unless otherwise indicated, are on a continuing operations basis. Refer to Note 8. Discontinued Operations of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for more information on the discontinued operation and transaction.

Mativ and its subsidiaries manufacture on three continents, conduct business in over 100 countries and operate 34 production locations worldwide. Our products are sold globally, though are most prevalent in North America and Europe with, to a lesser extent, Asia-Pacific and the rest of the world making up the remainder.

Our principal executive office is located at 100 Kimball Place, Suite 600, Alpharetta, Georgia 30009 and our telephone number is (770) 569-4229. Our stock is traded on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") under the symbol "MATV."

As a specialty materials manufacturing company, Mativ's primary processes consist of taking basic inputs, such as fibers, resins and chemicals, to create highly engineered media, such as nonwovens, films, specialty paper and netting. We then further process our media through coating, saturating, adhesive application and advanced converting processes to impart specific product attributes that are valued by our customers and customized to meet their unique needs.

Mativ's long-term growth ambition is focused on enhancing its position as a global specialty materials supplier of choice, driving performance by engineering unique, innovative solutions that connect, protect, and purify our world.

Fuel our customers' successes. We aim to serve leading customers in specialized, growing segments of materials markets, and look to create value for our customers by combining capabilities, technologies, and service platforms to produce tailored solutions that uniquely solve their most complex challenges. We have an agile supply chain and manufacturing base that enables us to efficiently produce customized offerings, often in smaller batches, that provide premium quality and unique attributes. We also stretch across layers of the value chain, combining our technologies to provide added value to our products and a more complete solution. Further, our products are specified and often undergo rigorous qualification cycles, and we are sought out as a partner for innovation opportunities. This creates deep customer relationships, which we believe fuels our ability to grow in our categories. Examples of this include our ability to bundle multiple components (media, support, cores and tubes) for water filtration, our ability to extrude and coat our advanced films for specified attributes, our ability to create unique colors, textures and finishes for premium packaging and consumer applications, and our ability to modify release characteristics for various adhesive applications.

Capture accelerated growth potential powered by key trends and innovation. We believe our businesses are aligned with key macroeconomic trends and end markets with strong growth outlooks. In addition to our existing product lines, we use these long-term trends to guide innovation efforts and bring to life solutions that support our customers' evolving needs. Key themes such as the demand for cleaner air and water, modern building practices, increased uses of adhesives, advancements in health and wellness and the desire for sustainable, eco-friendly alternatives, align with our offerings and provide long-term support for demand. In our filtration category, we produce multiple critical components of reverse osmosis filters supporting the increasing demand for clean water, as well as other highly engineered media to support rising needs for air and liquid purification in HVAC, industrial and life science applications. Our advanced films are used in automotive and building applications to safeguard surfaces from sunlight, sound, impact, water, and temperature—increasingly relevant to protect vehicles and buildings. Release liners are essential in the activation process of adhesives in both temporary and permanent connection applications, and are used in growing areas such as hygiene products for adult and feminine care, construction and labeling. Our healthcare lines support advanced healing, wound cleansing, skin-friendly adhesives, as well as device fixation for wearable medical devices—all influenced by an aging population and increased global focus on health and wellness. Our tapes and industrial products provide solutions used in growing areas such as cable harnesses and tape for electric vehicles, and protective coverings for cables used in infrastructure and construction. Lastly, our paper and packaging business addresses needs for sustainability and eco-friendly alternatives to plastic while supporting brand aesthetics and the customer experience.

Leverage economies of scale. We continue to execute on significant incremental revenue opportunities, as we look to identify strategic cross-selling opportunities and innovation in key categories like filtration, healthcare, release liners and tape. We also see geographic expansion as a growth opportunity to complement our expanded footprint in Asia, North America and Europe, demonstrated by recent growth investments in our sites in Italy, Canada, the United Kingdom and Mexico. Lastly, we are leveraging a more comprehensive value chain position, where we believe we can cross-source and present more complete offerings to our customers.

Transform the portfolio. We focus our investments, resources and efforts towards categories with the highest value-creation potential, focused on growth and margin-accretive opportunities. We actively manage elements of our portfolio that are non-core, margin dilutive or do not align with our growth ambitions to free up resources and to focus on more growth-oriented aspects of our portfolio. We have also closed or divested a number of smaller, non-strategic sites and redeployed capital to repay debt and invest in categories that are geographically expansive and products where we see additional opportunities for growth.

headings: Factors That May Affect Future Results
Risk Factors Summary
Our technological advantages are unlikely to continue indefinitely.
Effectively policing our domestic and international intellectual property and patent rights is costly and may not be successful.
Because of the geographic diversity of our business, we are subject to a range of international risks.
We are subject to risks related to our dependence on foreign imports and exports.
Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates could adversely impact our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
The Company could be subject to changes in its tax rates, the adoption of new U.S., or foreign tax legislation or exposure to additional tax liabilities.
We face competition from several established competitors and we have limited market transparency.
We are dependent upon the availability of credit, and changes in interest rates can impact our business.
Our failure to comply with the covenants contained in our credit agreements and other debt instruments could result in an event of default that could cause acceleration of our indebtedness.
Future dividends on our common stock may be restricted or eliminated.
Our internal and external expansion plans and asset dispositions entail different and additional risks relative to the rest of our business.
Divestitures or other dispositions could negatively impact our business, and contingent liabilities from businesses that we have sold or will sell could adversely affect our financial statements.
Impairment of goodwill has negatively impacted our results of operations. If goodwill is further or fully impaired in the future, our results of operations will be negatively impacted further.
We may not successfully integrate acquisitions into Mativ's operations and we may be unable to achieve anticipated cost savings or other synergies.
Our restructuring activities are time-consuming and expensive and could significantly disrupt our business.
Our financial performance can be significantly impacted by the cost and availability of raw materials and energy and we may have limited ability to pass through increases in costs to our customers.
The introduction of artificial intelligence ("AI") may present risks to our business.
We rely on a limited number of key employees and our failure to recruit and/or retain senior management and key employees globally could harm our business.

Public health emergencies or outbreaks of epidemics, pandemics, or contagious diseases have adversely affected, and could in the future, adversely affect our business and the business of our customers and suppliers.
Our business is subject to various environmental laws, regulations and related litigation that could impose substantial costs or other liabilities on us.
ESG issues may have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations, the desirability of our stock, and may damage our reputation.
Increases in costs of pension benefits may reduce our profitability and could impact our cash reserves.
We are subject to various legal actions and other claims.
Any loss or interruption of the operations of our facilities may harm our operating performance.
paragraphs: Many risk factors both within and outside of our control could have an adverse impact on our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows and on the market price of our common stock. While not an exhaustive list, the following important risk factors could affect our future results, including our actual results for 2025 and thereafter and could also cause our actual results to differ materially from those expressed in any forward-looking statements we have made or may make.
Material risks that may affect our business, operating results and financial condition include, but are not necessarily limited to, those relating to:
•Our technological advantages are unlikely to continue indefinitely; •Policing our intellectual property and patent rights is costly and may be unsuccessful;
•International geopolitical and other risks associated with our sales and operations outside of the United States, due to political unrest, terrorist acts, and national and international disputes;
•Risks related to our dependence on foreign imports and exports;
•Failure to comply with the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act ("FCPA") and other anti-corruption laws or trade control laws, as well as other laws governing our operations;

paragraphs: Throughout 2025, the U.S. government proposed the implementation of, or did implement, a number of tariffs on imports to the United States from a large number of countries, including baseline tariffs and additional individualized reciprocal tariff on certain countries with whom the United States has the largest trade deficits. Increased tariffs by the United States has led and may continue to lead to the imposition of retaliatory tariffs by foreign governments. Additionally, throughout 2025, the U.S. government announced and rescinded multiple tariffs on several foreign jurisdictions, which has increased uncertainty regarding the ultimate effect of the tariffs on economic conditions. Uncertainties about tariffs and their effects on trading relationships, including as a result of future developments, may impact the macroeconomic conditions in the markets in which we operate, and may do so with little to no advanced notice. Although we are continuing to monitor the impact of such announcements, as well as opportunities to mitigate their related impacts, costs and other effects associated with the tariffs remain uncertain.

We disclose those accounting estimates that we consider to be significant in determining the amounts to be utilized for communicating our consolidated financial position, results of operations and cash flows in the first note to our consolidated financial statements included elsewhere herein. Our discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations are based on our consolidated financial statements. Our consolidated financial statements are prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S., which require management to make estimates that affect the amounts of revenues, expenses, assets and liabilities reported and disclosure of contingencies. Changes in these estimates could have a material impact on our financial position, results of operations, and cash flows. We discussed with the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors the estimates and judgments made for each of the following items and our accounting for and presentation of these items in the accompanying consolidated financial statements:

Our income tax expense (benefit), deferred tax assets and liabilities, and liabilities for unrecognized tax benefits reflect management's best estimate of current and future taxes to be paid. We are subject to income taxes in the U.S. and numerous foreign jurisdictions.

Deferred income taxes arise from temporary differences between the tax basis of assets and liabilities and their reported amounts in the financial statements, which will result in taxable or deductible amounts in the future. In evaluating our ability to recover our deferred tax assets in the jurisdiction from which they arise, we consider all available positive and negative evidence, including scheduled reversals of deferred tax liabilities, projected future taxable income, tax-planning strategies, and results of recent operations. In projecting future taxable income, we begin with historical results adjusted for the results of discontinued operations and incorporate assumptions about the amount of future state, federal, and foreign pretax operating income adjusted for items that do not have tax consequences. The assumptions about future taxable income require the use of significant judgment and are consistent with the plans and estimates we are using to manage the underlying businesses. In evaluating the objective evidence that historical results provide, we consider three years of cumulative operating income (loss).

The calculation of our tax liabilities involves dealing with uncertainties in the application of complex tax laws and regulations in a multitude of jurisdictions across our global operations. Accounting Standards Codification Topic No. 740, Income Taxes ("ASC 740"), states that a tax benefit from an uncertain tax position may be recognized when it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained upon examination, including resolutions of any related appeals or litigation processes, on the basis of the technical merits. We record unrecognized tax benefits as liabilities in accordance with ASC 740 and adjust these liabilities when our judgment changes as a result of the evaluation of new information not previously available. Because of the complexity of some of these uncertainties, the ultimate resolution may result in a payment that is materially different from our current estimate of the unrecognized tax benefit liabilities. These differences will be reflected as increases or decreases to income tax expense in the period in which new information is available.

We accrue an estimated loss by taking a charge to income when the likelihood that a future event, such as a legal proceeding, will result in a loss or the occurrence of a liability is probable, and the amount of loss can be reasonably estimated. We disclose material contingencies if there is at least a reasonable possibility that a loss has been incurred. In determining whether a loss should be accrued, we evaluate, among other factors, the degree of probability of an unfavorable outcome and the ability to make a reasonable estimate of the amount of loss. Changes in these factors could materially impact our financial condition, results of operations, and our cash flows.
For further information, refer to "Litigation" in Part I, Item 3, "Legal Proceedings" and Note 18. Commitments and Contingencies of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.

Certain of our manufacturing processes are capital intensive; as a result, we make substantial investments in property, plant and equipment which are recorded at cost. Net property, plant and equipment comprised 30% of our total assets as of December 31, 2025. Property, plant and equipment is depreciated on the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets. Production machines and related equipment are not subject to substantial technological changes rendering them obsolete and are generally depreciated over estimated useful lives of 5 to 20 years. When indications of impairment exist, we assess the likelihood of recovering the cost of long-lived assets based on our expectation of future profitability and undiscounted cash flow of the related asset group. These factors, along with management's plans with respect to the operations, are considered in assessing the recoverability of property, plant and equipment. Changes in management's estimates and plans could significantly impact our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.

Goodwill is not subject to amortization and is tested for impairment at the reporting unit level annually, during the fourth quarter, specifically October 1, or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances indicate impairment may exist. The Company determines the fair value of its reporting units using the income approach based upon estimated future cash flows discounted at a rate commensurate with the risk involved or market-based comparables. The determination of the fair value using the income approach requires management to make significant estimates and assumptions related to forecasts of future cash flows and discount rates. Changes to the forecasted revenue growth, earnings before income taxes, depreciation and amortization ("EBITDA") and discount rate assumptions may result in a significantly different estimate of the fair value of the reporting units, which could result in a different assessment of the recoverability of goodwill or measurement of an impairment charge. During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2023, we performed interim quantitative goodwill impairment tests, which resulted in non-cash impairment charges of $411.9 million and $401.0 million, respectively. Refer to Note 9. Goodwill, of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information. The annual impairment tests performed on October 1, 2025, 2024 and 2023 resulted in no impairment charges. We continue to monitor the impact of the sustained impact of macro-economic conditions, an increasingly global competitive environment, along with continued volatility particularly in the construction and automotive sectors. Future deterioration in these conditions may require us to perform an interim quantitative impairment test in 2026.

paragraphs: 本年度10-K申報書包含根據1933年證券交易法第27A節（經修正）及1934年證券交易所法第21E節（經修正）所定義的前瞻性陳述。實際結果、表現或成就可能與前瞻性陳述中預期的有重大差異，原因包括多種風險、不確定性及其他因素。有關可能導致我們的結果、表現或成就與未來結果、表現或成就有重大差異的重要因素討論，請參閱下文第一部分，第1A項「風險因素」及第一部分，第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」。除非上下文另有說明，否則提及「Mativ」、「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」、「我們」或類似詞彙，均包括Mativ Holdings, Inc.及其合併子公司。
Mativ Holdings, Inc.為專用材料領域的全球領導者，透過工程創新解決方案，解決客戶最複雜的挑戰，以連接、保護並淨化我們的世界。Mativ透過我們的企業對企業及消費者產品品牌家族在全球進行製造。Mativ針對過濾、醫療保健、可持續包裝等多樣化且成長中的終端市場，追求高階應用。我們廣泛的技術組合結合聚合物、纖維及樹脂，以優化客戶產品在價值鏈各階段的表現。

Mativ於1995年在特拉華州成立，為Kimberly-Clark Corporation（「Kimberly-Clark」）的 wholly-owned subsidiary。1995年11月30日，Kimberly-Clark將其美國、法國及加拿大進行的煙草相關紙張及其他紙張業務轉讓給本公司，並將本公司所有普通股股份分發給股東（稱為「分拆」）。因此，本公司成為一間獨立上市的公司。隨後，本公司透過創新努力及多項收購，逐步擴大其業務範疇，以增加對過濾、專用薄膜、膠帶及醫療保健等相關產業的曝光度。

2022年7月6日，Schweitzer-Mauduit International, Inc.（「SWM」）完成一項涉及Neenah, Inc.（「Neenah」）的合併交易，根據該交易，SWM的 wholly-owned subsidiary 與Neenah合併，Neenah在合併後繼續作為SWM的直接且 wholly-owned subsidiary。自合併交易完成日起，SWM更名為Mativ Holdings, Inc.
2023年11月30日，我們完成將工程紙業務（「EP業務」）出售給Evergreen Hill Enterprise Pte. Ltd.（「Evergreen Hill Enterprise」）。隨著EP業務的出售（稱為「EP出售」），Mativ已停止參與煙草基產品市場。
自出售生效日起，EP業務被列為已終止營運，並對所有期間進行呈現。某些前期金額已回溯調整以反映這些變動。除非另有說明，合併財務報表及其附註均以持續營運為基礎。有關已終止營運及交易的更多資訊，請參閱財務報表附註第8項「已終止營運」。
Mativ及其子公司在全球三個大陸進行製造，業務遍及超過100個國家，並在全球擁有34個生產據點。我們的產品在全球銷售，但主要集中在北美和歐洲，亞太地區及其餘世界則佔較小比例。
本公司主要營業據點位於喬治亞州阿爾法雷塔市金巴爾廣場100號600室（100 Kimball Place, Suite 600, Alpharetta, Georgia 30009），電話為（770）569-4229。本公司股票於紐約證券交易所（"NYSE"）以符號"MATV"上市交易。
作為一家專業材料製造公司，Mativ 的主要製造流程係將基本原料，例如纖維、樹脂及化學品，轉化為高度工程化的媒體，例如非織布、薄膜、特殊紙張及網狀織物。我們再進一步對這些媒體進行塗佈、浸漬、黏合劑應用及先進轉換製程，以賦予產品特定的特性，這些特性受到客戶重視，並根據客戶的獨特需求進行客製化。
Mativ 的長期成長願景聚焦於強化其作為全球專業材料供應商的領導地位，透過工程獨特、創新性的解決方案，推動表現，以連結、保護及淨化我們的世界。

推動客戶的成功。我們致力於服務材料市場中專業且成長迅速的領域中的領先客戶，並透過結合能力、技術與服務平台，提供客製化解決方案，以獨特的方式解決客戶最複雜的挑戰。我們擁有靈活的供應鏈與製造基礎設施，使我們能高效生產客製化產品，通常以較小批次生產，提供高品質與獨特特性。我們也橫跨價值鏈的各層，結合技術以增加產品價值並提供更完整的解決方案。此外，我們的產品常被指定使用，並需經過嚴格的認證流程，我們也因此被視為創新機會的夥伴。這建立了深厚的客戶關係，我們相信這有助於我們在各個領域的成長。例如，我們能將多種零組件（媒體、支撐層、核心與管體）組合用於水過濾，我們能擠出並塗佈我們的先進薄膜以達到指定特性，我們能為高階包裝與消費應用創造獨特的顏色、紋理與外觀，以及我們能調整黏合劑應用的釋放特性。

把握由關鍵趨勢與創新驅動的加速成長潛力。我們相信我們的業務與關鍵總體經濟趨勢及成長前景看好的終端市場對齊。除了現有產品線，我們也利用這些長期趨勢來引導創新努力，並推出解決方案以支持客戶的不斷演進需求。例如，對潔淨空氣與水的需求、現代建築實踐、黏合劑使用量增加、健康與 wellness 的進步以及對可持續、環保替代方案的渴望，均與我們的產品線對應，並為長期需求提供支持。在過濾領域，我們生產多種反滲透過濾器的關鍵零組件，以支持潔淨水需求的增加，以及其它高度工程化的媒體，以支持空氣與液體淨化在 HVAC、工業與生命科學應用中的需求。我們的先進薄膜用於汽車與建築應用，以保護表面免受陽光、聲音、衝擊、水與溫度的影響—這在保護車輛與建築物方面越來越重要。釋放紙在黏合劑的啟動過程中至關重要，無論是臨時或永久連接應用，並用於衛生產品如成人與女性衛生用品、建築與標籤等成長領域。我們的醫療產品線支持先進的傷口治療、傷口清潔、皮膚友好的黏合劑，以及可穿戴醫療設備的固定裝置—all 受到人口老化與全球對健康與 wellness 關注度增加的影響。我們的膠帶與工業產品提供解決方案，用於電動車的電纜束與膠帶，以及用於基礎建設與建築的電纜保護覆蓋層。最後，我們的紙張與包裝業務解決對可持續與環保替代塑料的需求，同時支持品牌美觀與客戶體驗。
發揮規模經濟效益。我們持續執行重要的收入增長機會，並尋求識別過濾、醫療、釋放紙與膠帶等關鍵領域的戰略交叉銷售機會與創新。我們也認為地理擴張是成長機會，以補充我們在亞洲、北美與歐洲的擴張版圖，這從我們在義大利、加拿大、英國與墨西哥的廠區最近的成長投資可見一斑。最後，我們正在利用更完整的價值鏈地位，我們相信我們能進行跨源頭採購，並為客戶提供更完整的產品組合。
轉型產品組合。我們將投資、資源與努力聚焦於具有最高價值創造潛力的領域，專注於成長與毛利率提升的機會。我們積極管理與我們核心業務、毛利率或與我們成長願景不一致的產品組合元素，以釋放資源並專注於更具成長導向的產品組合方面。我們也已經關閉或出售了數個規模較小、非戰略性的廠區，並重新配置資金以償還債務，並投資於具有地理擴張潛力的領域與我們認為有更多成長機會的產品。

paragraphs: 2025 年期間，美國政府提出或已實施針對來自多個國家進口至美國的關稅，包括基準關稅及針對與美國有最大貿易逆差國家的額外個別對等關稅。美國提高關稅已導致並可能繼續導致外國政府實施報復性關稅。此外，2025 年期間，美國政府宣佈並撤銷多項針對多個外國管轄區域的關稅，這已增加對關稅最終對經濟條件影響的不確定性。對關稅及其對貿易關係影響的不確定性，包括因未來發展所導致的影響，可能影響我們營運市場的總體經濟條件，且可能在幾乎沒有預先通知的情況下發生。儘管我們持續監測這些公告的影響，以及尋求緩解相關影響的機會，但與關稅相關的成本及其他影響仍不確定。

我們揭露那些我們認為在決定用以溝通我們合併財務狀況、營運成果及現金流的金額時具有重大影響的會計估計。我們對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析係基於我們的合併財務報表。我們的合併財務報表係依照美國通用會計原則編製，這要求管理階層做出影響收入、費用、資產與負債金額的估計，並揭露潛在的或有事項。這些估計的變動可能對我們的財務狀況、營運成果與現金流產生重大影響。我們已與董事會審計委員會討論針對下列各項所做出的估計與判斷，以及我們在隨附合併財務報表中對這些項目之會計處理及呈現方式。
我們的所得稅費用（利益）、遞延所得稅資產與負債，以及未認列所得稅利益負債，反映管理階層對目前及未來需支付稅款的最佳估計。我們需納稅於美國及多個外國管轄區域。

遞延所得稅係因資產與負債的稅基與財務報表中所列示金額之間的暫時差異而產生，這些差異將導致未來產生應課稅或可扣減金額。在評估我們能否從產生這些遞延所得稅資產的管轄區域收回遞延所得稅資產時，我們會考慮所有可用的正面與負面證據，包括遞延所得稅負債的預期轉回、預測未來應稅所得、稅務規劃策略，以及近期營運結果。在預測未來應稅所得時，我們以歷史結果調整後的結果為起點，並納入對未來州、聯邦及外國預稅營運所得的假設，並調整那些不會產生稅務影響的項目。對未來應稅所得的假設需要使用重大判斷，且與我們用以管理相關業務的計畫與估計一致。在評估歷史結果所提供的客觀證據時，我們會考慮過去三年的累計營運所得（損失）。

我們計算所得稅負債的過程涉及處理在多個管轄區域的複雜稅法與規範應用上的不確定性。會計準則編碼主題第 740 號，所得稅（"ASC 740"），指出當稅務利益來自不確定稅務地位時，只有在該地位經審查後更可能被維持，包括解決任何相關上訴或法律程序的基礎技術優勢時，才能認列稅務利益。我們依照 ASC 740 規定，將未認列稅務利益列為負債，並在因評估新資訊而改變判斷時調整這些負債。由於某些不確定性的複雜性，最終解決結果可能導致支付金額與我們目前對未認列稅務利益負債的估計有重大差異。這些差異將在新資訊可得的期間內反映為所得稅費用的增加或減少。
我們在發生未來事件（例如法律程序）導致損失或產生負債的可能性為「很可能」，且損失金額可合理估計時，會計提預估損失，並在所得稅費用中列示。我們在有至少合理可能性已發生損失時揭露重大或有事項。在決定是否應計提損失時，我們會評估，包括其他因素在內，不利結果的機率與能否合理估計損失金額。這些因素的變動可能對我們的財務狀況、營運成果與現金流產生重大影響。
如需進一步資訊，請參閱第一部分，第三項「法律程序」及財務報表附註第 18 項「承諾與或有事項」的「訴訟」部分。

我們部分製造流程為資本密集型；因此，我們在廠房、設備與機械上進行大量投資，並以成本入賬。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，廠房、設備與機械淨值佔總資產的 30%。廠房、設備與機械以直線法按資產預計使用年限 depreciated。生產機械與相關設備不受重大技術變革影響而使其過時，通常以 5 至 20 年的預計使用年限 depreciated。當出現減值跡象時，我們根據對相關資產組未來獲利能力與未折現現金流的預期，評估長壽命資產成本能否收回。這些因素，加上管理階層對營運的計畫，會被考慮用以評估廠房、設備與機械的可收回性。管理階層估計與計畫的變動可能對我們的財務狀況、營運成果與現金流產生重大影響。

goodwill 不會計提攤銷，並於每年第四季，特別是在 10 月 1 日，或在事件或情勢變動顯示可能有減損時，於報告單位層級進行減損測試。本公司以收入法評估其報告單位之公允價值，基於預估未來現金流量，並以與風險相關或市場可比資料相符的折現率進行折現。以收入法評估公允價值的決定，需要管理階層針對未來現金流量預測及折現率做出重大估計與假設。預測收入成長、稅前盈餘、折舊及攤銷（"EBITDA"）及折現率假設的變動，可能會導致報告單位公允價值的估計值產生顯著不同，這可能會導致對 goodwill 可收回性評估或減損費用衡量的差異。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日結止之會計年度及 2023 年 12 月 31 日結止之會計年度，我們執行了中期定量 goodwill 減損測試，結果分別產生 411.9 百萬美元及 401.0 百萬美元的非現金減損費用。請參閱財務明細表註 9。Goodwill。有關更多資訊。於 2025 年 10 月 1 日、2024 年 10 月 1 日及 2023 年 10 月 1 日執行的年度減損測試，結果均未產生減損費用。我們持續監測總體經濟條件的持續影響、日益全球化的競爭環境，以及特別是在建築與汽車產業中持續的波動性。這些條件未來惡化可能需要我們在 2026 年執行中期定量減損測試。

paragraphs: 許多風險因素，無論是我們所能控制或無法控制，都可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果及現金流產生不利影響，並對我們普通股的市場價格產生影響。雖然這並非完整的清單，但以下重要的風險因素可能影響我們未來的結果，包括我們2025年及以後的實際結果，也可能導致我們的實際結果與我們已發表或可能發表的任何前瞻性陳述產生重大差異。
可能影響我們業務、營運結果及財務狀況的重要風險包括，但不僅限於：
•我們的技術優勢可能不會無限期持續；•執法我們的智慧財產權及專利權是成本高昂且可能失敗；
•與我們在美國境外銷售及營運相關的國際政治及其它風險，由於政治動盪、恐怖攻擊及國家與國際間的爭議；
•與我們對外進口及出口的依賴相關的風險；
•未能遵守美國外貿欺詐防治法（"FCPA"）及其他反貪污法律或貿易管制法律，以及其它規範我們營運的法律；
